newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian stocks rise in improved trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian stocks rise in improved trade.

text.p: Shares on the Jordanian stock exchange rose 0.26 percent on Sunday in improved trade buttressed by healthy outside buying, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.41 points to 156.64 points in trade worth 473,283 dinars ($668,478).
Heavily-weighted Arab Bank rose 0.5 dinars to 262 dinars in trade worth 104,810 dinars, or nearly a quarter of the total daily volume.
Brokers attributed a better performance to stronger outside demand for the traditionally popular industrials and banks than the market has seen last week.
"There was some buying on some positions that are expected to see foreign buying soon," said one broker.

Local fund managers say foreigners have been testing the market in the last few months by limited purchases on select industrials as they closely watch progress in IMF directed reforms before building up positions.

Brokers said they spotted clear demand on leading blue chip drug firms, such as Arab Pharmaceutical Chemicals and Arab Pharmaceutical Manufacturing which are forecast to perform well in 1997. They rose 0.03 dinars and 0.06 dinars respectively.
Investor attention continued on Jordan National Bank, which relisted last week after merging with the Business Bank, closing 0.01 dinars higher to 2.04 dinars after turnover of 42,143 dinars.
The shares rose as high as 2.10 dinars last Tuesday after the merger, which raised the capital of the combined bank above the Central Bank requirement of 20 million dinars.
Arab Potash Company was also busy, rising 0.04 dinars to 6.04 dinars in trade worth 35,000 dinars.
Overall 21 shares rose, eight fell and another seven traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 most-traded shares on the exchange rose 0.17 percent to 82.79 points, still 0.74 percent down from the start of the year.
